title: Your Brain Can't Feel Pain
sources: Brain tissue (parenchyma) has no nociceptors (pain receptors), so touching or cutting it does not hurt (StatPearls, 'Awake Craniotomy'; Penfield & Boldrey 1937)
In awake craniotomy, the scalp and skull covering are numbed with local anaesthetic; the patient stays awake so surgeons can map speech and movement areas (StatPearls, 'Awake Craniotomy')

Patients have talked, sung and played instruments such as guitar and violin during awake brain surgery (e.g. King's College Hospital 2020, violinist Dagmar Turner; Abdullah, guitar, Bengaluru 2021 reports)
Electrical stimulation of a language area during mapping can make the patient stop speaking (speech arrest), marking tissue to avoid (Ojemann et al. 1989)
Headache pain comes from pain-sensitive structures around the brain: the meninges, blood vessels and nerves, not the brain tissue itself (Ray & Wolff 1940; NIH)

lines.text: Doctors can poke your brain while you're awake, and it doesn't hurt at all.
lines.caps: Doctors can *poke | your *brain | while you're *awake | and it doesn't | *hurt at all

lines.text: That's because your brain has zero pain sensors of its own.
lines.caps: That's because | your brain has | *zero | *pain sensors | of its own

lines.text: It feels every pain in your body, but it can't feel itself.
lines.caps: It feels *every pain | in your *body | but it *can't | *feel itself

lines.text: So surgeons just numb the skin and skull, then open it up.
lines.caps: So surgeons | just *numb | the skin and *skull | then *open it up

lines.text: And the patient stays awake, talking, or even playing guitar.
lines.caps: And the patient | stays *awake | *talking | or even | playing *guitar

lines.text: If they touch a spot and the patient stops talking, they stay away from it.

lines.text: And headaches? Those come from the nerves around your brain, not the brain itself.
